File:crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:473
Decision: Direct-chat dedup uses optimistic locking: create the object first, then re-fetch and check for duplicates; if a race produced duplicates, pick the lexicographically smallest id as the winner and destroy the others, reporting alreadyExists to the losers.
Why good: Avoiding a serialised check-then-create removes a TOCTOU window without requiring backend-level transactions or a unique-constraint mechanism. The winner/loser selection rule (min id) is deterministic, so every concurrent requester converges to the same canonical object and no duplicate survives. The pre-batch hoisted fetch (O(1) instead of O(n) per-create fetches for the common non-concurrent path) keeps the fast path cheap while the post-create re-fetch only pays the extra round-trip when something was actually created.
title: GOOD: optimistic create-then-validate dedup for Direct chats
